name: xxh32
description:
32-bit xxHash (XXH32) — the classic 32-bit member of the xxHash family. Fast and well-distributed; use when 32 bits is enough — for in-memory hashtables, lightweight checksums, or short-lived bucket assignment.

Accepts an optional `UINTEGER` seed. Prefer `xxh3_64` when you don't have a specific reason to use the 32-bit format — XXH3 is faster on modern hardware and offers more headroom against collisions.

name: xxh64
description:
64-bit xxHash (XXH64). The original 64-bit xxHash — broadly supported across language bindings and on-the-wire identical to xxHash 0.6.x callers.

Pick `xxh64` when you must match an existing XXH64-based system; otherwise `xxh3_64` is faster on modern CPUs.

name: xxh3_64
description:
64-bit xxHash3 (XXH3_64) — the modern xxHash variant tuned for vectorized CPUs (SSE2/AVX2). Faster than `xxh64` on virtually all modern hardware, especially for short inputs, with comparable distribution quality.

This is the recommended general-purpose 64-bit non-cryptographic hash for partitioning, sharding, deduplication, and as input to probabilistic filters in bitfilters.

examples.description: Hash several columns as one key (row hashing)

name: xxh3_128
description:
128-bit xxHash3 (XXH3_128) returned as a `UHUGEINT`. The wider hash space dramatically reduces accidental-collision probability for very large keyspaces (billions of distinct keys).

Use when 64 bits feels tight — content fingerprints, dedup keys at scale, or any place a 64-bit birthday-bound starts to matter. For a portable hex digest instead of a number, use `xxh3_128_hex`.

For stored-key compatibility, this numeric function keeps its historical half ordering. Its formatted hex is not canonical; use `xxh3_128_hex` on corrected builds, or exchange the two 16-character halves of its zero-padded 32-character hex.

name: xxh3_128_hex
description:
128-bit xxHash3 returned as a 32-character lowercase hex string in canonical xxHash byte order (`high64 || low64`), as defined by the xxHash specification.

Matches the digest produced by `XXH128_canonicalFromHash` in C, `xxhash.xxh3_128().hexdigest()` in Python, and `xxhash-rust` when formatted as hex. Use it when the hash needs to be a string — Redis keys, filenames, or a fingerprint shared with non-SQL code.

The `v1.5` source fix dated October 7, 2026 corrects earlier reversed-half output, including build `0dec806`. The DuckDB 2.0 builds in the Query.Farm repository include it; community packages for DuckDB 1.5 may lag; `xxh3_128_hex('hello')` must return `b5e9c1ad071b3e7fc779cfaa5e523818`. Previously stored affected hex digests require a one-time half swap. Numeric `xxh3_128` results remain unchanged.

name: rapidhash
description:
RapidHash — a 64-bit non-cryptographic hash designed for exceptional speed while keeping competitive distribution quality. Frequently the fastest 64-bit hash in published benchmarks on modern x86_64.

Reach for `rapidhash` when `xxh3_64`'s throughput isn't quite enough, or when most of your hashed inputs are very short integers and you want the lowest per-call latency. As with the rest of this extension, this is **not** cryptographically secure — use `crypto` for digests and signatures.

name: murmurhash3_32
description:
32-bit MurmurHash3. Battle-tested across distributed systems — variants of MurmurHash3 underpin hash partitioning in Apache Cassandra, Apache Spark, and many other tools.

Choose `murmurhash3_32` when you need cross-system compatibility with an existing MurmurHash3-32 consumer. For new in-DuckDB workloads, `xxh3_64` is generally faster.

name: murmurhash3_128
description:
128-bit MurmurHash3 — the **x86 variant**. Returns a `UHUGEINT` covering both 64-bit halves of the hash.

Included for compatibility with consumers that specifically expect the x86 128-bit form. On modern 64-bit hardware, `murmurhash3_x64_128` is generally the right pick.

name: murmurhash3_x64_128
description:
128-bit MurmurHash3 — the **x64 variant**. The standard 128-bit MurmurHash3 form on 64-bit platforms; this is what most modern consumers (including Apache Cassandra's `Murmur3Partitioner` and Apache Spark's default hash partitioner) actually use.

Returned as a `UHUGEINT`. Use this when DuckDB needs to produce hashes that match what another system has already computed for the same key.

name: rapidhash_micro
description:
RapidHash Micro — the upstream compact RapidHash variant with a smaller code footprint. It returns the same value as `rapidhash` for inputs up to 80 bytes and a different value for longer inputs.

Use it only to match a system that hashes with `rapidhashMicro`; otherwise prefer `rapidhash`.

examples.description: Same as rapidhash for short input

name: rapidhash_nano
description:
RapidHash Nano — the smallest upstream RapidHash variant. It returns the same value as `rapidhash` for inputs up to 48 bytes and a different value for longer inputs.

Use it only to match a system that hashes with `rapidhashNano`; otherwise prefer `rapidhash`.

examples.description: Same as rapidhash for short input

name: wyhash
description:
64-bit [wyhash](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash), final version 4 with its original default secret — the version implemented by Java's [hash4j](https://github.com/dynatrace-oss/hash4j) (`wyhashFinal4`). Later upstream releases (4.2+) changed the default secret and therefore every hash value, so check which version a system uses before comparing.

Accepts an optional `UBIGINT` seed.

name: komihash
description:
64-bit [komihash](https://github.com/avaneev/komihash), version 5 — a fast, high-quality hash whose output has been stable since 5.0 and matches [hash4j](https://github.com/dynatrace-oss/hash4j)'s `komihash5_0`.

Accepts an optional `UBIGINT` seed.

name: siphash24
description:
SipHash-2-4, the standard [SipHash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SipHash), returning the 64-bit result as `UBIGINT`. The optional `key` is a `UHUGEINT` whose 16 little-endian bytes are SipHash's 128-bit key; without a key, all key bytes are zero — which matches ClickHouse's `sipHash64` of a String.

With a secret key, SipHash resists hash-flooding: an attacker who doesn't know the key can't craft inputs that collide. It is still not a MAC or digest — use [crypto](/products/extensions/crypto) for those.

examples.description: With a 128-bit key (key bytes 00, 01, …, 0f — the SipHash test key)

name: siphash13
description: SipHash-1-3 — the faster, reduced-round SipHash used by Rust's standard library and CPython 3.11+ for string hashing. Same key handling as `siphash24`: the optional `UHUGEINT` key supplies the 128-bit key as its 16 little-endian bytes.

examples.description: With a 128-bit key (key bytes 00, 01, …, 0f — the SipHash test key)

name: crc32c
description:
CRC-32C (Castagnoli) checksum as `UINTEGER` — the checksum used by iSCSI, ext4, Google Cloud Storage objects and many storage and wire formats. `crc32c('123456789')` is the standard check value `0xE3069283`.

The optional second argument continues a previous checksum: `crc32c(b, crc32c(a))` equals the checksum of `a` followed by `b`, so you can checksum data that arrives in pieces.

name: fnv1a_32
description: 32-bit [FNV-1a](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fowler%E2%80%93Noll%E2%80%93Vo_hash_function). Simple and widely embedded, but slower and weaker than modern hashes — use it to match an existing FNV-1a key. FNV-1a has no seed.

name: fnv1a_64
description: 64-bit [FNV-1a](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fowler%E2%80%93Noll%E2%80%93Vo_hash_function). Use it to match an existing FNV-1a key; for new work prefer `xxh3_64`. FNV-1a has no seed.

name: farm_fingerprint
description:
FarmHash Fingerprint64 as a signed `BIGINT` — the same value as BigQuery's [`FARM_FINGERPRINT`](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/hash_functions#farm_fingerprint) for the same `STRING` or `BYTES`. Accepts `VARCHAR` or `BLOB`.

Use it to reproduce BigQuery fingerprints, sampling splits (`MOD(ABS(FARM_FINGERPRINT(id)), 10)`) and keys in DuckDB.

name: spark_hash
description:
Spark's [`hash()`](https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/api/sql/index.html#hash): Murmur3 x86_32 with seed 42, returning a signed `INTEGER`. Takes one or more values; each value's hash seeds the next and `NULL`s are skipped, exactly as Spark does. Spark's string and binary hashing mixes trailing bytes non-standardly, so this differs from `murmurhash3_32`.

Values are hashed by Spark's type rules: `BOOLEAN`, `TINYINT`/`SMALLINT`/`INTEGER`/`DATE` as int, `BIGINT`/`TIMESTAMP` as long, `-0.0` folded into `0.0`, `DECIMAL` by unscaled value, and `LIST`/`ARRAY`/`STRUCT` element by element. Types Spark doesn't have (unsigned integers, `UUID`, `MAP`, ...) are rejected. Spark's bucket id is `pmod(hash(cols), n)`.

name: spark_xxhash64
description: Spark's [`xxhash64()`](https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/api/sql/index.html#xxhash64): XXH64 with seed 42, returning a signed `BIGINT`, with the same multi-value seeding, `NULL` skipping and type rules as `spark_hash`.

name: kafka_murmur2
description: Kafka's `murmur2` hash of a serialized record key (`VARCHAR` as UTF-8 bytes, or `BLOB`), as a signed `INTEGER` — the hash Kafka's default partitioner applies to keyed records.

name: kafka_partition
description:
The partition Kafka's default partitioner assigns a keyed record: `toPositive(murmur2(key)) % partitions`. Use it to predict which partition a key lands on, or to co-partition DuckDB output with a topic.

The key is the record key's serialized bytes — a `VARCHAR` is hashed as UTF-8, which matches Kafka's `StringSerializer`. A `NULL` key returns `NULL`, because Kafka doesn't hash records without a key. `partitions` must be between 1 and 2147483647.

examples.description: Partition for a key on a 12-partition topic

name: clickhouse_cityhash64
description: ClickHouse's [`cityHash64`](https://clickhouse.com/docs/sql-reference/functions/hash-functions#cityhash64) of a String: CityHash64 from CityHash v1.0.2, the version ClickHouse ships, as `UBIGINT`. Accepts `VARCHAR` or `BLOB`. ClickHouse hashes numbers and multiple arguments differently, so only string and binary inputs are supported. For ClickHouse's `sipHash64` of a String, use `siphash24` without a key.

name: iceberg_bucket
description:
The partition Apache Iceberg's `bucket[N]` transform assigns a value: `(murmur3_x86_32(value) & Integer.MAX_VALUE) % N`, using the Iceberg spec's encoding of each type. Use it to predict which bucket partition a row lands in, prune files by bucket, or write data partitioned the way an Iceberg table expects.

Accepts the types Iceberg can bucket: integers up to `BIGINT` (every width hashes alike), `DECIMAL`, `DATE`, `TIME`, `TIMESTAMP` at any precision, `TIMESTAMPTZ`, `VARCHAR`, `BLOB` and `UUID`. `BOOLEAN`, `FLOAT`, `DOUBLE` and other types are rejected, as Iceberg rejects them. A `NULL` value returns `NULL` (Iceberg's null partition). `buckets` must be between 1 and 2147483647.

examples.description: Bucket of a string in a bucket[16] partition
int and long values land in the same bucket

name: iceberg_hash
description: Iceberg's 32-bit bucket hash (spec Appendix B) as a signed `INTEGER`: MurmurHash3 x86_32 with seed 0 over Iceberg's encoding of the value — integers as 8-byte little-endian longs, `DECIMAL` as the minimal big-endian bytes of its unscaled value, dates as days, times and timestamps as microseconds (nanosecond timestamps floored), strings as UTF-8 and UUIDs in big-endian order. `iceberg_bucket` is this hash's low 31 bits modulo the bucket count.

name: jump_hash
description:
[Jump consistent hash](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.2294) (Lamping and Veach): assigns a 64-bit key to one of `buckets` buckets so that growing from n to n + 1 buckets moves only about 1/(n + 1) of the keys — all of them into the new bucket — where `hash % n` would move almost every key. Use it to reshard with minimal data movement.

The key is a `UBIGINT` or `BIGINT`, read as its 64 bits; hash the value first, e.g. `jump_hash(xxh3_64(x), n)`. Returns the bucket as `INTEGER` from `0` to `buckets - 1`, the same bucket Guava's `Hashing.consistentHash` returns. `buckets` must be between 1 and 2147483647.

examples.description: Growing to 17 shards keeps the key or moves it to shard 16
